title: DP on Trees
tagline: Compute each node's answer from its children — subtree DP and rerooting.

intuition.analogy: A company org chart: each manager's headcount equals the sum of their reports' headcounts plus one. You can only know a manager's total after every report has reported up — bottom-up aggregation.
paragraphs: Tree DP solves problems where a node's answer depends on the answers of its subtrees. Because subtrees are independent, a single post-order DFS computes everything: visit children first, then combine their results at the parent.

Many problems carry a small state per node — e.g. 'best if this node is included' vs 'best if excluded' (House Robber III), or counts, sums, and depths. The combine step is where the actual recurrence lives.

When the answer is needed for every node as a root (not just one root), the rerooting technique computes the rooted answer once, then transfers information from parent to child in a second DFS to adjust each node's perspective in O(n) total.
intuition.keyIdea: Post-order DFS aggregates child results into each node; rerooting extends per-node answers to all roots in O(n).

steps.title: Define the per-node state
steps.detail: Decide what each subtree returns — a single number, or a tuple like (best including node, best excluding node).

steps.title: Write the combine rule
steps.detail: Express the parent's state from its children's states. This recurrence is the crux of every tree-DP problem.

steps.title: Aggregate post-order
steps.detail: DFS down, compute children, then combine. Track a global answer if the problem asks for a path/optimum across the tree.

steps.title: Reroot if needed
steps.detail: For 'answer for every root' questions, do a second DFS pushing the complement information from parent to each child.

complexity.timeReason: Each node combines a constant amount of child information once.
complexity.spaceReason: Recursion depth equals the tree height.

pitfalls: Returning the global answer from the recursion instead of the per-node state needed by parents.
Rerooting bugs: mixing up which neighbour's contribution to exclude when moving the root.

dryRun.clickMoment: Each node keeps two numbers, not one. Carrying both 'include' and 'exclude' lets the parent pick freely — that extra state is what makes tree DP expressive.

problems.title: House Robber III
problems.statement: Max sum with no two directly-linked nodes chosen.

approach: Each node returns two values: the best total if we rob it (val + skip children) and the best if we skip it (max of child's rob/skip).
The answer at the root is max(rob, skip). Classic tree DP with a pair return.

problems.title: Binary Tree Cameras
problems.statement: Minimum cameras to monitor all nodes.
problems.hint: Three states per node: covered+camera, covered+no-camera, not-covered. Greedy bottom-up.

approach: Post-order with three states per node: 0 = needs coverage, 1 = covered without a camera, 2 = has a camera.

If any child needs coverage, place a camera here (state 2). If any child has a camera, this node is covered (state 1). Otherwise it needs coverage (state 0). Count cameras; cover the root if it ends in state 0.

problems.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
problems.statement: Count nodes ≥ every ancestor on their path.
problems.hint: Carry the running path maximum downward.

approach: A node is good if no node on the path from the root to it has a greater value. Carry the running maximum down the recursion.
Increment the count when the current value is >= the path maximum, then recurse with an updated maximum.

problems.title: Distribute Coins in Binary Tree
problems.statement: Minimum moves to give each node exactly one coin.
problems.hint: Each edge carries |subtree balance|; sum these in post-order.

approach: Each node must end with exactly one coin. A subtree's 'balance' = total coins - node count; coins equal to that balance must flow across the edge to the parent.
Sum the absolute balances of all edges — each unit is one move. Post-order returns the running balance.

problems.title: Sum of Distances in Tree
problems.statement: For each node, the sum of distances to all others.
problems.hint: Classic rerooting: compute for the root, then adjust per child in a second DFS.

approach: Rerooting in two DFS passes. First pass (post-order) computes subtree sizes and the answer for the root: sum of depths.

Second pass (pre-order) shifts the root along each edge: moving from parent u to child v adds (n - size[v]) nodes one step farther and brings size[v] nodes one step closer, so ans[v] = ans[u] + n - 2·size[v].
